newsitem.title: USA: Fedex says no open-skies without cargo deal.
newsitem.headline: Fedex says no open-skies without cargo deal.

text.p: Federal Express Corp does not expect there will be a new "open-skies" aviation pact between the United States and the UK without an agreement covering cargo, Fedex chairman Frederick Smith said.
"This is not an issue for the major players in the UK," he told journalists here on Wednesday.
A further round of talks between U.S. and British officials on the new aviation pact are scheduled to start in Washington on February 4.
"The restrictive policy on cargo rights (by the UK) has been very deleterious. Look at how continental European airports, for example Schiphol, have gained traffic at the UK's expense," Smith added.
"UK exporters and importers who rely on air transport have been unable to get the services they need to be competitive," he said.

The Scottish electronic industry in particular has been strongly complaining about the situation and "the only real opposition to a deal on air cargo comes from small cross-Channel operators," he added.

"A broad agreement on cargo open skies -- between the UK and the U.S. -- will be good for the UK, though it may be harmful to some European airports which have profited from the UK's restrictive policy," Smith said.
